name: Copper glycinate
description: Copper glycinate (CAS 18253-80-0 ), also known as cupric glycinate hydrate, is a chelated copper-amino acid complex used as a bioavailable copper source across nutritional, agricultural, and pharmaceutical applications. Its chelated form improves copper absorption compared to inorganic copper salts, making it a preferred choice for formulators targeting efficient mineral delivery in various industrial sectors. In dietary supplements and functional foods, it is used to fortify products where copper deficiency correction or antioxidant enzyme support is the primary formulation goal for the end user. Animal feed manufacturers incorporate it as an organic trace mineral source, particularly in poultry, swine, and aquaculture feeds where improved bioavailability translates to better growth outcomes. Pharmaceutical formulators use it in mineral supplement preparations where chelated copper is specified for enhanced gastrointestinal tolerance and superior metabolic absorption rates in patients. In food fortification, it serves as a copper source in products requiring clean-label or amino acid-chelated mineral declarations, meeting strict regulatory requirements for food safety. The product is typically supplied as a crystalline powder or fine solid. It is available in feed-grade and nutritional supplement grades, with specifications aligned to industry standards. Buyers should confirm purity levels and copper content per lot, as these vary by manufacturer. Quality may be verified against standards such as FCC or USP depending on the grade.
